visuals.heading: Every Postgraduate Route, Compared

items.text: Eight routes, compared on real entry requirements, real time, and real outcomes.
A PhD is only for people who want to become professors.
An MBA is not a science-specific route, but enough science graduates consider it that it deserves an honest place on this list.
Our strongest suggestion: treat roughly 10% of your family's total realistic education budget as the strict default ceiling for a single postgraduate course, including an MBA.

blocks.heading: Use the Four Questions Before You Commit

items.text: Eight routes across five subjects is still too many to compare in your head at once.

Do you want the slow, deep, deliverable-light rhythm of a PhD, the exam-and-batch structure of an MBA, the numbers-under-pressure grind of actuarial exams, or the faster, project-based rhythm of a certification.
A route with a great ceiling that fights how you actually like to work will not survive the years it needs from you.

blocks.heading: Proofs Before You Spend Money or Years

items.text: The four questions above helps you compare routes on paper.
The three proofs make you test the route in the real world before you commit an entrance-exam preparation year or several years of postgraduate study to it.
Do not lock in a multi-year plan, a PhD registration, or an education loan before passing all three steps.

visuals.heading: Honest Answer Before the List

figures.label: Monthly Internship Stipend
figures.source: A PhD that pays a Rs 42,000/month stipend and leads to a research career is not automatically worse than an MBA that costs Rs 15 lakh, if research genuinely fits how you want to spend the next several years. The reverse is just as true. The real question is which route fits your specific subject, your financial runway, and how fast you need income, not which one sounds the most respectable.

figures.label: Estimated Time Required
figures.source: This is the most common and realistic industry pivot for a Biology, Biotechnology, or Life Sciences postgraduate who does not want a 5-6 year PhD timeline. Entry as a clinical trial assistant or coordinator starts modest, but a Clinical Research Associate role clears Rs 3-9 LPA within a couple of years, with pharmacovigilance and regulatory tracks growing from there.

blocks.heading: Routes If You Studied Maths or Statistics

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: Actuarial science has one of the steepest documented salary curves of any postgraduate route in this guide, each set of two to three IAI exams cleared adds roughly Rs 3-8 LPA, but it requires years of sustained exam discipline, not a single degree.

figures.label: Typical Salary Range
figures.source: A Maths, Statistics, or Physics base makes the coursework considerably easier and the eventual salary range (commonly Rs 6-15 LPA at entry) considerably more reliable.

figures.label: Total Course Duration
figures.source: The realistic pay curve moves slowly at entry (Rs 2.4-4.5 LPA) but climbs meaningfully once you are inside a Clinical Research Associate or regulatory role, particularly with added training in FDA, EMA, or ICH-style global standards.
